reasons.P1-02 packages/kernel/trust-kernel/src/i: HOT ZONE. Written from `git show 05c22146ef -- packages/kernel/trust-kernel/src/index.ts` (+42/-1): `createTrustKernel` takes a new `config: TrustKernelConfig` carrying `trustAnchors`, a module-private `CONFIGURED_ANCHORS` WeakMap keyed by the handle holds them, and `configuredTrustAnchors` is a new export. reasons.P1-10 packages/plugin/plugin-manifest/sr: P1-01's `MigrationDeclaration` gains `module`, `reversible` and `backup`. Extending the existing declaration rather than adding a second manifest is the whole point of the bridge: a plugin author writes one `dsh` block, and the upgrade reads what they wrote. HOT ZONE by ownership -- the type is P1-01's -- so the change is additive and the three fields are optional at the type level, with the real requirement (module implies the other two) enforced in the validator where a relation between fields can be stated.

Where the new requirement is enforced: a step that ships a `module` must declare `reversible` and `backup`, and a `backup` outside the declared vocabulary is refused. Misconfiguration fails loud at the manifest read rather than at the upgrade that trusted it. reasons.P1-10 packages/storage/storage-json/src/: The JSON backend's migration facet: snapshot as a copy beside the unit, switch as a rename with the replaced document kept as the rollback target, plus `stampedVersion`, `digestUnit`, `readSnapshot` and `exportUnit`. It reads and writes the SAME document `kv.open` parses, through `format.ts`'s own `serialize` -- an earlier version invented `{ version, records }`, which this backend never writes, and every case over it passed because each seeded the invention.
reasons.P1-10 packages/storage/storage-sqlite/sr: The SQLite backend's migration facet, created by this epic. One database holds every unit, so a snapshot cannot be a file copy: it is a sidecar database carrying just that unit's rows, produced by ATTACH inside the live database's own transaction, and a switch is a row replacement in a single transaction. A `:memory:` database exposes no facet at all, because it has no directory to hold a sidecar -- an upgrade on that medium is refused by name rather than failing partway through.

reasons.P2-02 packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-: Written from `git show 62cdc3ddd9 -- packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts` (+14/-0): the loop now reads `ctx.get('capabilityTokens')`, awaits `whenSessionToken(agent.id)`, and puts the token and, on failure, `issuanceError(agent.id)` onto every tool execution. reasons.P4-08 packages/workflow/workflow-worker-: HOT ZONE. From `git show 07acd35c6e -- packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/src/index.ts`: `start` and the new async `resume` both delegate to one private `launch`, the journal directory is derived from the storage root, and `childFinished` reads the child's DURABLE session. Shared with P4-07, whose lease acquisition is in the same `launch` body and is unchanged by this.

The reconciliation itself: which recorded steps a resumed run may reuse, and the script digest `admitResume` compares. New file; the plan named the journal package but not the engine-side half that reads it back.

`WorkerInit` gains `reusable`, the only channel by which a reconciled decision reaches the worker: `workerData` is structured-cloned at spawn, so anything the script's `agent()` consults has to be there before the thread exists.
reasons.P4-08 packages/workflow/workflow/src/ind: HOT ZONE. From `git show 07acd35c6e -- packages/workflow/workflow/src/index.ts`: `WorkflowEngine` gains the abstract `resume(runId, request): Promise<WorkflowRun>`. A Service Definition change, so every implementation must answer it — three test stubs did. §12.23 chose this over making `start()` async for callers that have no run to resume.
reasons.P4-09 packages/subagent/subagent/src/des: The durable subagent descriptor, touched because a detached run delegates from ITSELF and a continuable child must re-derive from the same session after a restart. The registry's files[] names the workflow packages, not the subagent seam that persists the delegation -- but `delegatingSession` has to live where the descriptor is written and parsed, and the field was silently dropped on every cold resume until it was added to `parseSubagentDescriptor`'s field-by-field rebuild as well as to the whitelist. Frozen in P4-09 U.5.
reasons.P4-09 packages/workflow/tool-workflow/sr: The model-facing consumer of must[2]. The clause is about a run a TURN starts and a later turn collects, and the only thing a turn can call is the tool: `startDetached` and `attach` existed on the seam with no product path reaching either, so the clause's consumer half had not arrived. `detached`/`attach` are added here, and `script`/`meta` stop being schema-required because an attach call carries neither. The registry named the engine packages, not the tool that fronts them.
reasons.P4-09 packages/workflow/workflow-filesys: §12.48-A(2). The producer P4-09 never had: a saved workflow is a file under the harness home, read at boot and registered through the engine's own admission. `registerDefinition` had 0 production callers before this, so nesting was reachable only from a test. New package, so it is outside the registry's file lists by construction.
The loader's cases, including the real-composition one that mounts the actual worker-thread engine rather than a stub sink.
The new package's compiler face and project references.
reasons.P4-09 packages/workflow/workflow-registr: Nesting-depth decisions, which is the subject of the U-stage clause.
The registry store the P-stage clause persists through.

§12.48-A. `declaresNestedCall` matched only a quoted FIRST argument, `workflow('name')`, so it could not fire on `workflow({ name, digest })` — the shape a nested run actually carries. The self-recursion refusal was therefore a false negative in exactly the case it exists for. The file is the registry's C/F-stage file; this is a correction the Provider wiring cannot ship without.
reasons.P4-09 packages/workflow/workflow-worker-: HOT ZONE. From `git show d3a23a5e2c -- packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/src/host.ts`: `WorkerRun` gains `onNestedStart`/`nest`, a `nestedRuns` set, and a `NestingPort` constructor argument; `cancel()` gains the `cancelPropagationForNested` block. Shared with P4-07 (the lease) and P4-08 (the journal), whose code in this file is untouched by the diff — the nesting additions sit beside them and change neither.

§12.48-A. The engine held its registered definitions in a bare `Map`, so `admitRegistration`, `isSelfRecursive` and the whole `DefinitionRegistry` had zero production callers and the digest a caller supplied was stored without ever being recomputed. The registry now holds them, which is where must[0]'s version pinning and acceptance[0]'s real meaning acquire their consumer. The registry's U-stage list named `runtime.ts`/`session.ts`, not this file.

The NestedStart / NestedSettled / NestedRefused messages. A nested run has to be started by the HOST, so the worker's request and the host's single reply need wire shapes; the file's existing tags are untouched.

`ChildPort` gains `startNested` and `NestedStartRequest` is declared. The port is how a script's hook reaches the host, and the plan named the runtime and session files without naming the seam between them.
reasons.P4-09 packages/workflow/workflow/src/ind: The workflow Service Definition, touched to declare `attach(runId)` as an abstract member (P4-09 must[2] semantic 5). The registry's files[] names `workflow/src/types.ts` but not the seam's own class; declaring the method on the concrete engine instead would have made it reachable only by a caller holding the implementation type, which is the present-but-unreachable shape this epic was reopened for. Three stub engines in other packages implement it as a result, which is the compiler recording that re-attachment is part of what an engine IS. Frozen in P4-09 U.6.
reasons.P4-11 packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts: The LLM service's dispatch, touched because must[2]'s breaker has to refuse BEFORE the adapter is reached and this is the only place that can. The registry's files[] names the retry packages, not the service they guard; `llm-retry` was the alternative and is the wrong one -- it decides whether to retry and never issues a request, so a breaker consulted there would refuse a retry while letting a first attempt through to a dead endpoint. `LlmAdapter.endpointUrl` is added in the same file because only an adapter knows the endpoint a route resolves to.
reasons.P4-11 packages/reliability/retry-cockati: The circuit-breaker PROVIDER: one cockatiel policy per (provider, baseUrl, model) behind this epic's own `CircuitBreakerContract`. The registry's files[] names the decision package and the LLM service it guards, not the package that holds the adopted runtime — and the make-vs-use record says cockatiel is adopted rather than reimplemented, so the adoption has to live in a file this epic owns or the decision is unverifiable. Separate from `packages/reliability/retry` on purpose: the contract must stay mountable without cockatiel, and a composition that mounts neither keeps its pre-epic behaviour.
reasons.P4-11 packages/reliability/retry/src/pro: The breaker's Service Definition — `BreakerDestination`, `BreakerOpenError` and the single `execute(destination, operation, classify)` operation. Split from `index.ts` because the destination identity is the epic's own decision (provider + baseUrl + model) while the counting behind it is cockatiel's: the file is what lets the adopted runtime be swapped without moving any consumer. The registry's files[] named the decision modules before the seam existed.
reasons.P4-11 packages/reliability/retry/src/roo: Which run a retry is charged to. The registry's files[] names the classifier and the budget but not the attribution between them, and must[1] is entirely about attribution: a Run is 1:1 with a session, so charging the retrying agent's own run gives a parent and each child an independent allowance -- the stacking the clause names. Kept pure over a caller-supplied lookup so the decision package stays free of the agent and session packages.
reasons.P4-11 packages/reliability/retry/src/usa: Where one run's retry spending is kept, and the self-provided service that mounts it. `admitRetry` is pure and returns the usage a caller should store, so two layers can only share a total by reading and writing the SAME store -- a per-layer copy is the duplication this epic ends. The allowance lives on the store rather than in each caller's parameters for the same reason: two layers passing their own budgets would share a total and disagree about the ceiling.
reasons.P4-12 packages/core/tools/src/external-e: The reserve/confirm pair and the refusal text, moved out of the agent loop so BOTH dispatch paths reach one implementation. The plan named the ledger and the native loop; it named no home for a rule the code-mode path also has to obey, and writing it twice is the shape BLOCKED-136 records.
reasons.P4-12 packages/core/tools/src/index.ts: Passes the registry's own context to the code-mode transport, which is what the reservation reads the ledger from. A sub-dispatch's agent handle need not carry a context, and reading one there threw inside `commit` — surfacing as hung cases rather than an error.
reasons.P4-12 packages/core/tools/src/ptc.ts: The code-mode dispatch site: where a sub-call reserves before running and settles after. Without it acceptance[0]'s at-most-once held for a tool called natively and not for the same tool called from a code-mode program.

reasons.P6-01 packages/core/session/src/known-ev: The registration side of this epic's own session event. memory/workspace-rebuilt is a new SessionEventMap member, and a SessionEventMap member is required-on-read by default: a build that does not know the type refuses the whole log. reasons.P1-07 packages/workspace/workspace-trust: The durable form of the trust binding. must[0] requires the state to be bound to a canonical realpath and an inode/volume identity, and a binding that dies with the process is not a binding: before this file existed, a second process re-read the operator grants against whatever directory then stood at the granted path, so a directory replaced while nothing was running came back trusted (BLOCKED-199). The registry named the decision files and the provider, and not the shape those records take on disk, because in the plan the binding was not yet durable. It is a source file rather than a test fixture because the schema is what validates a document written by an earlier build, and it carries the one conversion between the stored row and the vocabulary record — a brand and an exactOptional distinction the validator cannot express.
reasons.P1-07 packages/interaction/user-approval: The approval request gained an optional `subject` so a decision that is not about a tool call can say what it IS about — for a trust question, which workspace and which state. P1-07 is the consuming epic and made the addition; P2-11 owns this surface and is NOT_RUN, so the change is recorded in evidence-P2-11.md as purely additive: `toolName` stays required, the published runtime invariant that holds it non-empty is unchanged, the outcome vocabulary is unchanged, and 268 passing cases across every live P2-04 frozen command were compared by NAME before and after. The registry could not have named this file: in the plan, must[2] had no interaction and therefore no request to carry.
reasons.P1-07 packages/workspace/command-workspa: The host user's own route to `trusted-execute`. must[2] requires the upgrade to be completed by a host-user interaction, and the measurement showed the obvious place cannot work: project skills are not listed at `trusted-read` — their names and descriptions are text the project supplied — so the agent never reaches for one and there is no point of use at which it could be asked. The request must therefore come from the user, which makes it a command. The registry named the provider and the decision package and not this, because in the plan the interaction did not exist at all.
